messages:
maya: Quick FYI — noticed a bunch of requests showing up as project=org-default in the console after the canary. Looks like service-account-issued tokens are being attributed to the org instead of the project. Anyone seen this? :eyes:
leo: I saw a spike in staging yesterday, same pattern. repro steps?
tess: what does the auth path look like? is the claim being parsed or are we relying on headers?
maya: repro: create project `proj-456`, mint SA token via exchange, call /v1/generate with that token. Console shows billing/project = org-123 (the org default) instead of proj-456. Header capture from the recorder:
```http
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...
X-Org-ID: org-123
X-Project-ID: proj-456
```
samir: interesting — the edge auth parses token claims and adds `origin.claims` but we also honor `X-Project-ID` header as an override. last deploy changed header stripping for refresh flows though.
leo: so which wins today? header or token claim?
tess: current console attribution code checks headers first, then token claims, then org default. That was to support partner proxies setting a header.
maya: problem is the exchange flow seems to call internal upstream without the header (we strip it), so the header path disappears and the code falls back to org default instead of claim.
leo: easy mitigation: change precedence to claim > header > default for the canary so SA flows attribute to claims (sa:proj-456). That avoids breaking partners that intentionally inject headers?
tess: but some partners rely on header override specifically to impersonate cross-project calls — flipping precedence could be surprising.
samir: proposal: make precedence configurable per route with telemetry. attribution.precedence = ["claim","header","default"] for internal api routes (exchange, proxy), keep external-facing routes unchanged. Also emit telemetry tag `auth_source` (claim|header|default) per request. Sample 1% in prod.
maya: sounds good. We should also add token_type (user/sa/ephemeral) and token_kid to the telemetry so we can correlate.
deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-routing-v2 -> staging at 2025-06-15T14:02:00Z :rocket:
leo: small UX ask from product: console request inspector should show `auth_source` and a tooltip explaining precedence. Can we ship that in the same roll?
nora: yes, UX can add a tiny hover explanation — won't block rollout. I'll wire a note in the inspector: "Auth attribution uses token claims when available; header overrides are special-case".
tess: rollout plan: enable configurable precedence on staging now, do 1% sampling in prod next week, monitor metrics: `project_unattributed_rate`, `auth_source_change_rate`, and `project_mismatch_count`.
maya: I'll add a unit test in the exchange path to ensure we don't drop x-project-id on refresh accidentally. Opening a PR now.
samir: I'll extend telemetry schema to include `auth_source`, `token_type`, `token_kid`. Also add an alert: if `project_unattributed_rate` > 0.5% sustained for 5m, page eng-platform.
maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/482 — includes precedence toggle + tests.
leo: :thumbsup: once staging looks good we can promote.
nora: thanks all — I'll update the product rollout board and add the tooltip copy.
maya: one more note: let's capture a small debug log when attribution falls back to default so we can trace affected requests without logging full tokens. Something like: `auth.attribution=default reason=missing_claim_or_header kid=<kid>`
samir: agreed, but redact sensitive bits. only emit kid and request id.
tess: I'll coordinate the canary and the dashboard. thanks team.
